exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
being the smaller or bigger twin
cohort: 719 pairs of twins born between 1990 and 2017 at the University Centre of Obstetrics and Gynecology in Wroclaw, Poland, after excluding cases with unknown chorionicity/amnionicity, monochorionic/monoamniotic pregnancies, stillbirths, and fetal defects.
finding: Twins with a birth weight difference of less than 15%, second-born twins, and those delivered by cesarean section were more likely to receive a good Apgar score at 5 minutes.
mod_finding: A higher proportion of twins delivered by cesarean section received a good Apgar score compared to those delivered vaginally.
